title: lore check reports a profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget (DEC-11: warning for one release, then the error)
description:
A profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget makes lore's pack assembler drop declared sources, mark the pack truncated true with per-source omitted-by-budget, and EXIT 0. So a repository whose profiles declare more than their budgets hold runs narrowed packs and nothing says so -- a silent absence with a green exit. Found in the field, not theorised: ward-cli WCLI-25 (opum-ai/ward-cli#43) measured 16 of 16 packs complete before a change and 16 of 16 truncated after it, all at exit 0, with the documentation pack dropping its threat-model ADR on a generic task. The condition is capacity-driven -- declared sources against max_tokens -- and the same across four task texts, so it is checkable statically: no task string, no compile.

RULED by DEC-11 (opum-ai/opum-agent, .quest/planning.json at origin/main 0c61324, read there rather than taken on relay): the operator decided first-party via AskUserQuestion in the opum-doc session, 2026-09-29, relayed by opum-doc (correlation R-2026-09-29-01) and received by opum-agent at about 02:45Z. Option A: GATE IN lore check. A profile whose declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget becomes a lore check error, shipped FIRST AS A WARNING for one release so external users are not turned red without notice, and THEN AS THE ERROR. It authorises the pair release the change rides in (constitution Article 3). OPAG-714 is the paired audit half -- sdlc-audit reports truncated packs across the fleet -- and proceeds either way; it is fleet-only coverage, which is why the gate lives in lore. SCOPE: any lore check behaviour other than warning-then-error on capacity is a design change and goes back to opum-agent for the operator, not a reuse of this approval.

Filed on opum-agent's dispatch (cross-session, 2026-09-29T02:51Z). Queued after LCLI-639 and LCLI-640; it does not preempt either.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `lore check` reports, from the profile declaration alone, that a profile's declared sources cannot fit its max_tokens budget -- naming the profile, its budget and the sources that cannot fit -- and ships as a WARNING in the next pair release (DEC-11)
The flip to an error is a one-line, reviewable change, landed in the release AFTER the warning's and held as an explicit release step (DEC-11's warning-then-error ordering), not left to memory

A test proves the check warns on a deliberately over-declared fixture profile and stays silent on one that fits; a mutation control shows the capacity comparison is the clause doing the work (removing it reddens exactly the capacity cases); and the check prints how many profiles it read, so its clean answer cannot be a zero-input artifact
lore-cli's own profiles do not warn -- OPAG-33's swept budgets hold, with LCLI-640's documentation profile included -- captured on the current bundle
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the change

implementationNotes:
MEASUREMENT carried over from LCLI-640 (2026-09-29), recorded here rather than left on the other record because AC4 depends on that profile's budget and because it is a trap for this task's implementer. Nothing here starts this task or changes its scope.

The capacity condition this task gates on is static and task-independent, but a PER-TASK omission is NOT evidence of it. The two must not be conflated when the check is implemented.

Measured on the bundle as LCLI-640 leaves it, with the new documentation profile at max_tokens 20000 and 10 declared sources, compiled against four realistic documentation tasks: the omitted-source counts were 5, 1, 0 and 0. Two of the four tasks omitted NOTHING, so that profile is not over capacity -- and the first task nonetheless omitted five declared sources (reference/lore-cli-documentation-ownership, reference/operate-autonomous-lore-cli-documentation-campaigns, adr/0010-multi-consumer-docs-layer, reference/consumer-compatibility, runbooks/agent-profile-operation, every one scoring at or below 4.16). That is the task-ranked mechanism working as designed, not a capacity defect. An implementation that compiles a pack for some task string and warns when anything comes back omitted-by-budget would therefore false-positive on lore-cli's own documentation profile and would fail AC4. The check has to compute capacity from the declaration alone -- declared sources against max_tokens, with no task string and no compile -- which is what the description already specifies. This measurement is the reason to keep it that way.

SECOND MEASUREMENT, which the capacity comparison must survive: the omission curve is NOT monotone in max_tokens, so "does everything fit" is not a monotone predicate in the budget. On the first task above, 20000 selected 23 of 80 ranked blocks while 20500 selected only 5; the larger budget admitted one large high-scoring block whole ("Release publishing > Steps > 3. Cut a release", score 8.480238) and it consumed the room several smaller blocks had been using. The full thirteen-budget table is on LCLI-640's evidence note. A capacity test expressed as a monotone size comparison is unaffected by this; a capacity test measured by compiling packs is not, and can move the wrong way as the budget is raised.
